transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been struggling to cope with the aftermath and painful, intrusive memories of a traumatic event that happened about two years and five months ago. These memories just keep forcing their way into my mind, and I can't seem to stop them. It has been incredibly hard to deal with, and I really need some help.

Since this event occurred over two years ago, have you also been experiencing significant avoidance of reminders, negative changes in your mood or thoughts, or feeling constantly on edge or easily startled?

Yes, for the last two and a half years, I've tried desperately to avoid any thoughts, people, or places that remind me of what happened. I feel completely numb inside, unable to experience happiness, and I'm constantly on edge and living in fear. It feels like I can never let my guard down.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Posttraumatic Stress Disorder, Acute Stress Disorder, Adjustment Disorder]. Acute Stress Disorder is ruled out because the symptoms have persisted for over two years (the diagnosis requires symptoms for 3 days to 1 month). Adjustment Disorder is ruled out because the patient meets the full criteria for PTSD, which takes precedence. Given the duration and the specific cluster of intrusive, avoidant, negative cognitive/mood, and hyperarousal symptoms, PTSD is the clear diagnosis.
